Purpose: Create a shared understanding of the workshop objective and explain how OKRs will be used during the session.
Instructions:
Introduce the purpose of the workshop.

Explain the difference between Objectives and Key Results.

Set expectations for the session and explain that the goal is to align around a single objective and measurable indicators of success.

Review the agenda and answer any questions before beginning.
Facilitator Notes:
Keep the introduction short and focused.

Avoid teaching OKRs in depth.

The goal is to create enough understanding for participants to confidently take part in the activity.

Purpose: Review proposed objectives and ensure everyone understands the options being considered.
Instructions:
Review each submitted objective one at a time.

Clarify wording where needed.

Ensure participants understand what each objective is trying to achieve before moving on.
Facilitator Notes:
Do not debate which objective is best at this stage.

Focus only on understanding and clarification.

Purpose: Group similar objectives together and identify common themes.
Instructions:
Ask participants to group similar objectives together.

Discuss emerging themes and identify overlaps.

Create labels for each cluster once patterns begin to emerge.
Facilitator Notes:
Avoid naming themes too early.

Focus on patterns and relationships rather than perfect categorisation.

Purpose: Select a single objective that the group believes should be the primary focus.
Instructions:
Review the objective themes.

Allow participants a short period to reflect independently.

Run a blind vote.

Reveal results simultaneously.

If there is no clear outcome, facilitate a short discussion and conduct a second round of voting.
Facilitator Notes:
Avoid debate before voting.

Blind voting helps reduce hierarchy and groupthink.

The objective is alignment, not unanimity.

Purpose: Generate possible measures that indicate progress towards the selected objective.
Instructions:
Ask participants:

How would we know we are making progress?

Capture every suggestion.

Encourage quantity over quality.

Avoid evaluating metrics while they are being generated.
Facilitator Notes:
Keep participants focused on measurable signals rather than solutions or outputs.

Push for observable outcomes where possible.

Purpose: Group similar metrics together and identify the strongest indicators of success.
Instructions:
Group similar metrics into clusters.

Remove duplicates.

Identify common themes and discuss which measures best indicate progress.
Facilitator Notes:
Focus on clarity and relevance.

Do not spend time debating exact numbers at this stage.

Purpose: Identify the most meaningful metrics that will become Key Results.
Instructions:
Review the grouped metrics.

Ask participants to independently vote for the metrics they believe best represent progress towards the objective.

Reveal votes simultaneously.

Select the highest scoring metrics for the next step.
Facilitator Notes:
Limit the final selection to a small number of metrics.

Focus on quality and relevance rather than quantity.

The chosen metrics should be understandable and measurable.

Purpose: Convert selected metrics into measurable Key Results.
Instructions:
Review each selected metric.

Turn each metric into a measurable target.

Capture the baseline if known and define a target outcome.

Ensure each Key Result can be objectively measured.
Facilitator Notes:
Avoid vague targets.

Push for measurable and time-bound outcomes.

Challenge targets that are either unrealistic or too easy to achieve.

Purpose: Confirm alignment on the final Objective and Key Results and agree ownership.
Instructions:
Review the final Objective and Key Results.

Agree who owns each Key Result.

Capture any follow-up actions and review dates.

Confirm commitment from the group before closing the activity.
Facilitator Notes:
Do not end the workshop without clear ownership.

Ensure actions are assigned to individuals rather than teams.

Finish with clarity on what happens next and when progress will be reviewed.

Purpose: Create a shared understanding of the problem that will be explored during the activity.
Instructions:
Present the problem statement to the group.

Review any relevant evidence, examples or observations.

Ensure everyone agrees on the problem being explored before moving on.

Capture the final wording of the problem so it remains visible throughout the activity.
Facilitator Notes:
Spend time clarifying the problem if needed.

A poorly defined problem will lead to poor root-cause analysis.

Focus on observable issues rather than assumptions about causes.

Purpose: Identify the most immediate cause of the problem.
Instructions:
Ask the group:

"Why is this problem happening?"

Capture all responses.

Discuss the responses and agree on the most likely cause.

Record the agreed cause clearly as it will become the input for the next why.
Facilitator Notes:
Encourage participants to use evidence and observations where possible.

Avoid jumping to solutions.

Focus on understanding causes rather than assigning blame.

Purpose: Explore the underlying cause of the first identified cause.
Instructions:
Take the agreed cause from Why #1.

Ask the group:

"Why is this happening?"

Capture responses.

Discuss the responses and agree on the most likely underlying cause.

Record the agreed cause so it can be explored further in the next step.
Facilitator Notes:
Keep digging beneath symptoms.

Challenge assumptions and ask for evidence where possible.

Avoid accepting the first answer without discussion.

The objective is to move closer to the root cause.

Purpose: Continue exploring deeper causes to move beyond surface-level explanations.
Instructions:
Take the agreed cause from Why #2.

Ask the group:

"Why is this happening?"

Capture responses.

Discuss the responses and agree on the most likely underlying cause.

Record the agreed cause so it can be explored further in the next step.
Facilitator Notes:
Watch for participants repeating previous answers in different words.

Encourage the group to think about systems, processes and behaviours.

If the discussion moves towards solutions, redirect the conversation back to causes.

Purpose: Explore deeper systemic causes and identify factors contributing to the problem.
Instructions:
Take the agreed cause from Why #3.

Ask the group:

"Why is this happening?"

Capture responses.

Discuss the responses and agree on the most likely underlying cause.

Record the agreed cause so it can be explored further in the next step.
Facilitator Notes:
By this stage the group should be moving beyond symptoms and into organisational, process or behavioural causes.

Keep asking for evidence and examples.

Purpose: Identify the root cause or causes that the group believes are driving the problem.
Instructions:
Take the agreed cause from Why #4.

Ask the group:

"Why is this happening?"

Capture responses.

Discuss the responses and agree on the most likely root cause.

Record the final root cause clearly and visibly.
Facilitator Notes:
Do not force the group to stop at exactly five levels if a root cause has already emerged.

Equally, do not stop too early if the group is still discussing symptoms.

Purpose: Review the chain of causes and confirm the root cause or causes identified by the group.
Instructions:
Review each why and its corresponding answer.

Walk the group through the full chain of reasoning.

Confirm agreement on the root cause or causes before moving on.
Facilitator Notes:
Look for gaps in logic.

Challenge conclusions that are not supported by evidence.

It is acceptable to identify multiple root causes if they are connected.

Purpose: Agree how the root causes will be used to inform future activities or decisions.
Instructions:
Review the identified root causes.

Agree any immediate actions, owners and follow-up activities.

Capture next steps and ensure accountability before closing the activity.
Facilitator Notes:
Five Whys should rarely end without action.

Ensure the outputs are carried into the next activity, such as Problem Statement, How Might We or Opportunity Mapping.

Purpose: Create a shared understanding of the evidence, research and observations that led to the workshop.
Instructions:
Review the available research, insights, feedback and evidence.

Present key findings and observations.

Allow participants to ask clarifying questions.

Ensure everyone has a common understanding of the challenge before defining the problem.
Facilitator Notes:
Focus on facts and evidence rather than opinions.

Avoid discussing solutions.

The goal is to establish a shared understanding of the situation.

Purpose: Generate multiple perspectives on what the problem actually is.
Instructions:
Ask participants to individually write their version of the problem statement.

Encourage concise statements.

Capture all responses before discussing them.
Facilitator Notes:
Keep participants focused on the problem.

Do not allow solution statements.

Individual thinking before discussion usually produces better results.

Purpose: Identify common themes and patterns across the submitted problem statements.
Instructions:
Group similar problem statements together.

Identify recurring themes.

Discuss similarities and differences.

Create labels for each cluster.
Facilitator Notes:
Look for patterns rather than perfect wording.

Avoid jumping to conclusions too early.

The goal is to understand how the group views the challenge.

Purpose: Create a small number of candidate problem statements based on the themes identified.
Instructions:
Using the themes identified, ask participants to draft candidate problem statements.

Aim for clear, concise and evidence-based statements.

Capture all drafts before evaluating them.
Facilitator Notes:
Challenge vague language.

Ensure statements describe the problem rather than the solution.

Encourage participants to use evidence gathered earlier in the activity.

Purpose: Refine the strongest candidate statements and consolidate them into a shortlist.
Instructions:
Review the drafted problem statements.

Discuss strengths and weaknesses.

Combine similar statements and improve wording.

Reduce the list to a small number of strong candidates.
Facilitator Notes:
Review the drafted problem statements.

Discuss strengths and weaknesses.

Combine similar statements and improve wording.

Reduce the list to a small number of strong candidates.

Purpose: Align on the problem statement that will guide future activities.
Instructions:
Review the shortlisted problem statements.

Ask participants to independently vote for the statement they believe best represents the challenge.

Reveal votes simultaneously.

Select the winning statement or run a second round if needed.
Facilitator Notes:
The goal is alignment, not perfection.

If two statements are very similar, consider merging them before voting.

Capture the final agreed problem statement clearly and visibly.

Purpose: Ensure everyone understands the problem statement that will be used to generate opportunities.
Instructions:
Review the agreed problem statement.

Clarify any questions.

Ensure participants understand the challenge before moving into opportunity generation.
Facilitator Notes:
Keep this step brief.

The goal is alignment, not rewriting the problem statement.

Purpose: Generate multiple opportunity-focused questions from the problem statement.
Instructions:
Ask participants to rewrite the problem statement as a series of How Might We questions.

Encourage quantity over quality.

Capture all suggestions before discussing them.
Facilitator Notes:
Ask participants to rewrite the problem statement as a series of How Might We questions.

Encourage quantity over quality.

Capture all suggestions before discussing them.

Purpose: Identify patterns and common opportunity areas across the generated questions.
Instructions:
Group similar How Might We questions together.

Identify common themes and opportunity areas.

Label each cluster.
Facilitator Notes:
Focus on opportunities rather than solutions.

Avoid debating feasibility at this stage.

Purpose: Refine the strongest opportunity areas and remove duplicates or overlapping themes.
Instructions:
Review each opportunity cluster.

Discuss overlaps and similarities.

Merge related opportunities where appropriate.

Create a shortlist of the strongest opportunity areas.
Facilitator Notes:
Focus on opportunity quality rather than quantity.

Avoid moving into solution discussions.

Ensure the opportunities remain connected to the original problem statement.

Purpose: Align on the opportunity areas that should be explored further.
Instructions:
Review the shortlisted opportunity areas.

Ask participants to vote independently.

Reveal votes simultaneously.

Select the highest scoring opportunities for future exploration.
Facilitator Notes:
The objective is prioritisation, not perfection.

If there is no clear winner, facilitate a short discussion and vote again.

Purpose: Review the opportunities, ideas or initiatives that will be evaluated during the activity.
Instructions:
Review the list of opportunities.

Clarify any questions.

Ensure participants understand what each opportunity is before evaluation begins.
Facilitator Notes:
Keep discussion focused on understanding.

Do not begin evaluating opportunities yet.

Purpose: Establish a shared understanding of the evaluation framework.
Instructions:
Introduce the Impact Effort matrix.

Explain the two axes:

Impact
Effort

Review the criteria that will be used to assess opportunities.
Facilitator Notes:
Agree the criteria before evaluating opportunities.

Different interpretations of impact or effort can create unnecessary debate later.

Purpose: Evaluate and position opportunities based on their expected impact and effort.
Instructions:
Review each opportunity one at a time.

Discuss expected impact.

Discuss expected effort.

Place the opportunity on the matrix.

Repeat until all opportunities have been mapped.
Facilitator Notes:
Focus on relative comparison rather than perfect scoring.

Encourage evidence-based discussion where possible.

Avoid spending too much time on individual opportunities.

Purpose: Identify patterns and discuss what the completed matrix is revealing.
Instructions:
Review the completed matrix.

Identify opportunities that naturally group together.

Discuss patterns emerging across the map.

Highlight quick wins, strategic bets and low-value opportunities.
Facilitator Notes:
Focus on patterns rather than individual opportunities.

Encourage discussion around what the map is telling the team.

Purpose: Align on which opportunities should move forward.
Instructions:
Review the opportunities identified as strong candidates.

Ask participants to vote independently.

Reveal votes simultaneously.

Identify the highest-priority opportunities.
Facilitator Notes:
Use voting to reduce bias and avoid dominant voices driving the decision.

Focus on commitment rather than perfection.

Purpose: Agree the final recommendations and capture next steps.
Instructions:
Review the selected priorities.

Agree actions, owners and timelines.

Capture next steps and confirm accountability.
Facilitator Notes:
Ensure the workshop ends with clear ownership and agreed follow-up actions.

Avoid leaving priorities without accountability.

Purpose: Review the opportunities, ideas or initiatives that need to be prioritised.
Instructions:
Review all opportunities that have been brought into the workshop.

Clarify any questions.

Ensure everyone understands the options before prioritisation begins.
Facilitator Notes:
Focus on understanding rather than debating.

Keep the group aligned on what is being prioritised.

Purpose: Agree the criteria that will be used to evaluate and prioritise opportunities.
Instructions:
Discuss what makes an opportunity important.

Agree the prioritisation criteria.

Capture the criteria where everyone can see them before continuing.
Facilitator Notes:
Misaligned criteria create poor prioritisation.

Invest time here to create a shared understanding.

Purpose: Evaluate opportunities against the agreed criteria and identify relative priorities.
Instructions: Evaluate opportunities against the agreed criteria and identify relative priorities.
Facilitator Notes:
Encourage evidence-based discussion.

Focus on relative comparison rather than absolute scoring.

Avoid spending too much time debating a single opportunity.

Purpose: Review the emerging priority groups and identify patterns in the prioritisation.
Instructions:
Review the prioritised opportunities.

Group similar priorities together where appropriate.

Discuss patterns, dependencies and strategic themes.

Identify which opportunities appear most important.
Facilitator Notes:
Look for clusters and themes rather than focusing on individual items.

Encourage the team to discuss what the prioritisation is revealing.

Purpose: Align on the opportunities that should move forward.
Instructions:
Review the prioritised opportunities.

Ask participants to vote independently.

Reveal votes simultaneously.

Select the highest-priority opportunities.
Facilitator Notes:
Use voting to reduce bias and create transparency.

Focus on reaching alignment rather than achieving a perfect ranking.

Purpose: Capture actions, ownership and next steps for the selected priorities.
Instructions:
Review the selected priorities.

Agree actions, owners and timelines.

Capture next steps and confirm accountability.
Facilitator Notes:
Do not end the activity without clear ownership.

Ensure actions are assigned to individuals and have realistic deadlines.

Purpose: Create a shared understanding of the topic, process or team behaviour being reviewed.
Instructions:
Introduce the focus area being reviewed.

Explain the purpose of the activity.

Review any relevant context, evidence or observations.

Ensure everyone understands the scope before beginning.
Facilitator Notes:
Keep the discussion focused on the agreed topic.

Avoid moving into solutions at this stage.

Purpose: Generate ideas for what should start, stop and continue.
Instructions:
Ask participants to individually generate items for:

Start
Stop
Continue

Capture all contributions before discussion begins.
Facilitator Notes:
Encourage participants to think independently before discussing ideas.

Focus on behaviours, processes and ways of working.

Purpose: Identify common themes and patterns across participant responses.
Instructions:
Group similar responses together.

Identify recurring themes.

Label clusters and discuss common patterns.
Facilitator Notes:
Look for repeated issues and opportunities.

Avoid debating individual contributions.

Purpose: Refine the themes and identify the most important areas for action.
Instructions:
Review each theme.

Discuss overlaps and clarify wording.

Consolidate themes where appropriate.

Prepare a shortlist for prioritisation.
Facilitator Notes:
Focus on clarity and actionability.

Avoid introducing new ideas at this stage.

Purpose: Align on the most important themes that should be acted upon.
Instructions:
Review the shortlisted themes.

Ask participants to vote independently.

Reveal votes simultaneously.

Identify the themes that should move forward.
Facilitator Notes:
Keep voting focused on impact and importance.

Use a second round if results are unclear.

Purpose: Turn the selected themes into actions with ownership and accountability.
Instructions:
Review the selected themes.

Agree actions, owners and timelines.

Capture next steps and confirm accountability.
Facilitator Notes:
Do not finish the activity without clear ownership.

Focus on realistic actions that can be followed through.
